<header class="ws-head"><span class="ws-kicker">Day 2 · Technical module 5 · paired with M5</span><h2>Technical module 5<span class="ws-badge">Placeholder</span></h2></header>
<p class="ws-note"><b>Not written yet.</b> Until it is, this page shows what its paired policy module, <a href="workshop-m5.html">M5 Governance, decision rights and the legal basis</a>, asks of the technical side, as starting material.</p>
<h3>What M5 asks of the technical side</h3><div class="ws-cards"><div class="ws-card"><a class="ws-step" href="en/smart-trust-demo/journeys/smart-trust-demo/workshops/dpi-h-policy-track/walkthrough/J1/">J1</a><b>An Onesan baby is born in Taifafeki</b><p><span class="ws-t">What the system does</span>Credential issued to a child with no national ID.</p></div><div class="ws-card"><a class="ws-step" href="en/smart-trust-demo/journeys/smart-trust-demo/workshops/dpi-h-policy-track/walkthrough/J2b/">J2b</a><b>Registered at home, and referred</b><p><span class="ws-t">What the system does</span>Temporary id created at a home visit, offline.</p></div><div class="ws-card"><a class="ws-step" href="en/smart-trust-demo/journeys/smart-trust-demo/workshops/dpi-h-policy-track/walkthrough/J4.0a/">J4.0a</a><b>One phone holds the whole family’s records</b><p><span class="ws-t">What the system does</span>Parent holds the child's record on a shared device.</p></div><div class="ws-card"><a class="ws-step" href="en/smart-trust-demo/journeys/smart-trust-demo/workshops/dpi-h-policy-track/walkthrough/J4.0b/">J4.0b</a><b>Dad creates a link to share at the clinic</b><p><span class="ws-t">What the system does</span>Consent resource recorded; 4-digit passcode; 14-day expiry.</p></div><div class="ws-card"><a class="ws-step" href="en/smart-trust-demo/journeys/smart-trust-demo/workshops/dpi-h-policy-track/walkthrough/J4.1/">J4.1</a><b>A Taifafeki doctor sees the full history</b><p><span class="ws-t">What the system does</span>AuditEvent logged in Onesa on every access, including failed passcodes.</p></div></div>
<h3>Terms at those steps</h3><div class="ws-terms"><a href="glossary.html#term-electronic-immunization-registry" title="Records each person's doses. Often the first working part of a lifelong record.">Electronic immunization registry</a><a href="glossary.html#term-client-registry" title="The Client Registry is the national authoritative source of health-specific person identity. It is the foundational health-sector component that maintains a unique, verifiable identity record for every person who accesses or is eligible to access health services within a jurisdiction.">Client Registry</a><a href="glossary.html#term-facility-workforce-and-product-registries" title="Authoritative lists of health facilities, health workers, and products such as vaccines and their batches.">Facility, workforce and product registries</a><a href="glossary.html#term-dose-number-and-series" title="Which dose this is, out of how many in the schedule. Needed to work out what is due next.">Dose number and series</a><a href="glossary.html#term-batch-number" title="Identifies the production batch of a vaccine. Needed for recalls and safety checks.">Batch number</a><a href="glossary.html#term-verifiable-credential" title="A digitally signed statement, such as a vaccination record, that anyone can check is genuine and unaltered.">Verifiable credential</a><a href="glossary.html#term-digital-signature" title="A cryptographic seal made with the issuer's private key. Verifiers check it with the matching public key.">Digital signature</a><a href="glossary.html#term-public-key-infrastructure" title="The keys, certificates and rules that make digital signatures trustworthy.">Public key infrastructure</a><a href="glossary.html#term-issuer-holder-verifier" title="The three roles: who signs the credential, who keeps it, and who checks it.">Issuer · holder · verifier</a><a href="glossary.html#term-health-certificate-identifier" title="The unique ID of an issued certificate.">Health certificate identifier</a><a href="glossary.html#term-international-certificate-of-vaccination-or-prophylaxis" title="The &quot;yellow card&quot;. The digital ICVP is its signed, verifiable form.">International Certificate of Vaccination or Prophylaxis</a><a href="glossary.html#term-consent" title="A person's permission for their data to be used or shared. Rules for minors and dependants differ by country.">Consent</a><a href="glossary.html#term-civil-registration-and-vital-statistics" title="Birth registration can start a child's immunization record.">Civil registration and vital statistics</a><a href="glossary.html#term-point-of-service-application" title="Point-of-service applications are end-user application components (IT systems or software tools) used by individuals directly engaged in healthcare—such as clinicians, community health workers, and patients—that enable interaction with the broader healthcare ecosystem.">Point-of-Service Applications</a><a href="glossary.html#term-interoperability" title="Interoperability is the standards-based capability of heterogeneous information systems to communicate, exchange data, and use the exchanged information to execute functions effectively.">Interoperability</a><a href="glossary.html#term-digital-wallet" title="An app where a person holds their credentials. A signed paper QR code can play the same role.">Digital wallet</a><a href="glossary.html#term-personal-health-record" title="Health information the person can see and control, for example in a wallet or citizen app.">Personal health record</a><a href="glossary.html#term-lifelong-health-record" title="The Lifelong Health Record (LHR) is one or more governed data repositories, whether physically consolidated or virtually federated, that collectively maintain a longitudinal, person-centred record of an individual's key health information across care settings and over their lifetime.">Lifelong Health Record</a><a href="glossary.html#term-international-patient-summary" title="A standard minimal health summary, including immunizations, readable across borders.">International Patient Summary</a><a href="glossary.html#term-hl7-fhir" title="FHIR is a standard for healthcare data exchange, published by HL7®">Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources</a><a href="glossary.html#term-implementation-guide" title="A FHIR specification for one use case: profiles, codes and tests. It can be adopted rather than authored.">Implementation guide</a><a href="glossary.html#term-profile" title="A FHIR resource tailored to a use case, for example by making some fields required.">Profile</a><a href="glossary.html#term-procurement-conditions" title="Requirements written into tenders, such as conformance to the national IG, that steer what suppliers build.">Procurement conditions</a><a href="glossary.html#term-application-programming-interface" title="A defined, documented way for one system to ask another for data.">Application programming interface</a><a href="glossary.html#term-global-digital-health-certification-network" title="WHO Global Digital Health Certification Network. A trust network so countries can verify each other's health documents. Countries onboard per use case.">Global Digital Health Certification Network</a><a href="glossary.html#term-trust-list" title="A published list of keys accepted as valid issuers. The GDHCN shares these between countries.">Trust list</a><a href="glossary.html#term-health-information-exchange" title="The layer that routes data securely between systems.">Health information exchange</a></div>
